Claim 1 (Currently amended): A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of light pulses having a first speed; receiving a second sequence of light pulses from a vehicle; and transmitting a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 2 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 3 (Currently amended): The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 4 (Currently amended): The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having a third speed based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the third speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 5 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 6 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 7 (Currently amended): The method of claim 6, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 8 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 9 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from two or more vehicles, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 10 (Currently amended): The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses, and wherein the method is performed using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 11 (Currently amended): An apparatus, comprising: a processor; a memory, the memory storing instructions executable by the processor to: transmit a sequence of light pulses having a first speed; receive a second sequence of light pulses from a vehicle; and transmit a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the apparatus is configured to operate using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 12 (Currently amended): The apparatus of claim 11, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, and wherein the apparatus is configured to operate using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 13 (Currently amended): The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed, and wherein the apparatus is configured to operate using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 16 (Currently amended): The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed, and wherein the apparatus is configured to operate using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.

Claim 17 (Currently amended): The apparatus of claim 16, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network, and wherein the apparatus is configured to operate using a non-transitory computer-readable medium.
